claims.text: A strong low-field magnetocaloric response in rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys is driven by enhanced local magneto-elastic coupling.
Nano-scale compositional fluctuations produce enhanced local magneto-elastic coupling.
Nano-scale compositional fluctuations create regions with distinct magnetic exchange interactions.
The exchange-modified regions promote rapid spin reorientation near the magnetic transition temperature.
The proposed fluctuation-driven mechanism preserves rapid heat exchange, low hysteresis, and mechanical stability.
The initial alloy is a mostly uniform disordered solid-solution matrix containing nano-scale chemical variations and local lattice distortions.
Changing the concentration of a targeted transition metal can modulate the degree of nano-scale compositional fluctuation.
Nano-scale chemical fluctuations and associated lattice distortions mediate magnetostructural coupling.
Regions with modified exchange interactions lower the energetic barriers for spin reorientation near the magnetic transition.
Rapid spin reorientation produces an abrupt magnetization change and a strong magnetocaloric effect.
The proposed response occurs without substantial structural changes that would increase hysteresis or compromise mechanical integrity.
Relative to the baseline, adjusting the transition-metal concentration will sharpen the magnetization change.
Relative to the baseline, the modified alloy will show larger low-field adiabatic temperature and magnetic entropy changes.
The compositional adjustment will not reduce heat-exchange rate or increase hysteresis.
The baseline alloy has a moderate magnetocaloric response, a broad transition, and typical hysteresis.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply only within a narrow concentration window near the Curie temperature and at fields below approximately 1 T.
The mechanism may lose validity far from the Curie temperature or at fields substantially above approximately 1 T.
